Photograph: James Manning/PA James Cleverly James Cleverly resigns from shadow cabinet to run for mayor of London Shadow minister for housing, communities and local government to resign with immediate effect Sammy Gecsoyler Sat 29 Aug 2026 12.24 EDT First published on Sat 29 Aug 2026 11.25 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google James Cleverly has resigned from the shadow cabinet to run for mayor of London. The Tory heavyweight, who was once home and foreign secretary and is shadow minister for housing, communities and local government, told the Sunday Times he will resign with immediate effect. The MP for Braintree, who lost his bid to lead the Conservatives to Kemi Badenoch, is considered a more moderate voice in a party that has lurched to the right. On breaking the news to Badenoch, Cleverly told the Sunday Times: “She took it very well. Kemi has been very gracious.” He added: “Our route to getting Kemi in No 10 has got to be through success in London ,” he said. “It’s a business city, entrepreneurialism, arts, culture. I don’t buy the lazy idea that London is a Labour city. It represents the philosophical heart of the Conservative party.” Cleverly’s resignation comes ahead of the Conservative party conference in October where he is expected to make his case to party members. According to the Sunday Times, sources close to Badenoch said she was “gutted” about the news but added that “Kemi is delighted that someone of his calibre wants to put himself forward to be Conservative nominee for mayor of London.” Cleverly had kind words for Badenoch. “Frankly, Kemi is doing really well now. She’s getting great cut through. It took longer than any of us would have liked, but she’s getting it,” he said. Sadiq Khan is halfway through his third term as mayor. He has not stated whether he will run for a fourth term in the contest to be held in May 2028. Susan Hall was the Tory candidate in 2024 but lost to Khan who was declared the winner with 43.8% of the vote. If Khan does step down, the Labour MP for Brent Central and Brent South, Dawn Butler, is expected to throw her hat in the ring, having previously revealed her desire for the job. Cleverly is the most senior Tory politician to run for mayor of London in recent times. Making his bid, he said Khan was “asleep at the wheel” and accused him of using the role as a stepping stone for a higher-profile position. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to First Edition Our morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it matters after newsletter promotion “Sadiq has been trying to get out of that job for quite a while. He went in with the intention of doing what Boris [Johnson] did, using it as a high-profile platform to get him his next big job in government. There has been lots of posturing, very little delivery. Lots of picking rows with the president of America, less focus on bringing down street crime. It wouldn’t surprise me if he bows out for 2028. He’s lost the passion for the job.” Days before Keir Starmer stood down as prime minister, he handed Khan a peerage, potentially opening the door to him joining Andy Burnham’s cabinet in future. However, while Burnham and Khan have worked closely together over the years, and have a shared understanding of the challenges of devolution, it is understood Khan has told the former Manchester mayor that he has no wish to be a minister in his government. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c699.text: Image source, LightRocket via Getty Images Image caption, Poland said a Russian military Mi-8 helicopter - like the one seen in this archive photo - stayed in Polish airspace for 42 seconds By Jaroslav Lukiv Published 19 minutes ago Poland has said a Russian military helicopter briefly violated its airspace, forcing the Nato member to scramble fighter jets while ground forces remained on alert. Its military said the Mi-8 aircraft had crossed from the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad on Wednesday morning, penetrating Polish airspace to a depth of about 300 metres (328 yards) and staying for 42 seconds north of Braniewo. It said "the nature of the incident indicates that Russia is once again testing the readiness of our air defence". Moscow did not comment immediately. Poland and other European Nato members have recently said Russia may be preparing attacks to test their commitment to supporting Ukraine - Moscow denies this. Russian President Vladimir Putin has repeatedly said Moscow does not plan to attack Nato states. By contrast, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said this month that it was Europe that was constantly talking about preparing for war, and he warned: "If Europe attacks Russia, it will be a completely different war [from that in Ukraine], and it will be very short." Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and Moscow currently controls about 20% of Ukrainian territory, including the Crimea peninsula annexed in 2014. Europe targeted by spiralling campaign of sabotage - and Russia is the chief suspect Published 4 September In a statement, the Polish Army Operational Command said the brief incursion had happened at 11:08 (09:08 GMT), and the helicopter had been tracked by radar. Poland's air defence units were operating around the clock ready to "ensure the safety of Polish airspace", it added. A number of Russian drones and one unarmed Russian missile have landed in Poland since the start of Russia's invasion of Ukraine, which is not a member of Nato. Last week, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk suggested Russia was planning drone and missile strikes against Poland and other countries on Nato's eastern flank. "In recent weeks, the Russian hybrid threat against Europeans... has intensified," he said. "The intent is to intimidate us and break our effort to support Ukraine. The result will be the exact opposite. We are not intimidated because we know that our security today and tomorrow is at stake in Ukraine." French President Emmanuel Macron said shortly afterwards that his country had been targeted by Russian hybrid attacks in the past few weeks, vowing that this would not be left "without a response". Macron said he had already ordered a plan to protect the country's critical infrastructure and defence industry sites. Hybrid warfare or hybrid attacks are loose terms which tend to describe non-military methods, for example cyberattacks, sabotage or misinformation, designed to exert pressure and destabilise an adversary. These are quite often employed using proxies, but Russia always denies involvement in such attacks despite growing evidence to the contrary. There have recently been a number of suspicious fires and blasts at defence facilities in a number of European Nato members from Italy to Bulgaria to Estonia, with some of the affected countries blaming Russia. Earlier this month, Germany said Russia was responsible for August's drone attack at Leipzig airport - an accusation denied by Moscow as "absurd". And earlier this week, Lithuania's prime minister told the BBC that his country had already made evacuation plans in the face of threats from Russia, but added they would "not surrender" if attacked. Meanwhile in Ukraine, a Russian drone hit a passenger train near the border with Poland on 13 September shortly after former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson and top European security officials had passed through along the same line. Ukraine said the drone's target "could have been the diplomatic train", while the Russian military said only that it had struck "railway infrastructure". https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ckp8.text: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, A 37-year-old caretaker was killed at a primary school in a town north of Warsaw this week By George Wright Published 11 October 2026 Three violent attacks at Polish schools this week were driven by the "glorification of violence" online, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said. The attacks have left one woman dead and others injured, including children. "These are very often spontaneous actions inspired by online activity," Tusk said on Sunday, during a crisis meeting with security services. Police have arrested 117 people across the country for possession knives or other weapons, or for threatening to attack schools or fellow students, after searching tens of thousands of schools. A woman was arrested on Saturday after injuring three people while attacking a 17-year-old girl at an educational institution in the capital, Warsaw. It came a day after thousands of police visited schools across Poland, following two stabbing attacks earlier in the week, one of which led to the killing of a female caretaker. "We are not dealing with any group organized on a big scale," Tusk said on Sunday. "In the past years and months, we have noted - globally and in Poland - a rise in the fascination with violence," he added. The prime minister said the attacks were acts of "nihilistic violence" associated with the extreme right. "Some of the people detained are active in the ultraright environment," he said, adding that police had noticed a rise in online searches of Nazi content as well as of "mass killers who have become idols online". On Wednesday, a 19-year-old student attacked and injured nine people at a vocational school in the central Polish province of Mazovian. A day later, the 37-year-old caretaker was killed after a 15-year-old entered a primary school in LeszczydÃ³Å-Nowiny, north of Warsaw. Interior Minister Marcin KierwiÅski also said a 17-year-old was detained in the town of Sierpc, north-west of Warsaw, after allegedly stating "on school grounds that he planned to do something... dangerous - that he intended to harm someone". Thousands of Polish âpolice officers visited schools nationwide to try to reassure pupils after the stabbings sparked rumours of a "Bloody Friday" of more attacks stemming from a supposed online challenge. Meanwhile, Polish security services convened a special meeting on Sunday after receiving information about a potential attack on Tusk and Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, a spokesperson said. A special services spokesman said officials were treating the threat as "deadly serious".
